skill.name: file-uploads
skill.description: Guidance for building secure file upload workflows with cloud storage, presigned URLs, multipart uploads, and image optimization.
skill.summary: Helps developers design secure, scalable file upload and cloud storage flows.
skill.author: sickn33

finding_verdicts.reason: The path traversal string appears in a cautionary example that explains why user filenames are dangerous. The surrounding guidance recommends sanitizing filenames and generating safe names.

The line only throws an Invalid file type error after magic-byte validation fails. It does not perform reconnaissance, filesystem access, or data collection.

content.value_statement: File upload systems are easy to break with unsafe filenames, fake content types, or oversized files. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical upload patterns for safer cloud storage.
actual_capabilities: Explains secure file type validation with magic-byte checks.
Recommends upload size limits for server and client workflows.
Shows safer filename handling to prevent path traversal.
Guides use of S3 and Cloudflare R2 presigned URLs.
Covers multipart uploads and large file handling patterns.
Highlights cache controls for private presigned URL responses.
limitations: It provides guidance, not a complete storage integration.
It does not verify provider IAM policies or bucket permissions.
It does not replace application-specific security testing.
It may need adaptation for each framework and storage provider.

use_cases.title: Secure image upload flow
use_cases.description: Design an upload path that validates real file types, limits size, and stores safe object names.

use_cases.title: Direct-to-storage uploads
use_cases.description: Plan presigned URL uploads that avoid server buffering and reduce application load.

use_cases.title: Private file delivery review
use_cases.description: Check cached responses, URL expiry, and access patterns before serving private files.

prompt_templates.title: Review an upload plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my file upload plan for unsafe filenames, fake content types, missing size limits, and storage risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a presigned URL flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a presigned URL upload flow for S3 or R2 with size limits, safe object keys, and private file handling.

prompt_templates.title: Harden an existing endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this upload endpoint for path traversal, content validation, memory use, and cache exposure. Recommend focused fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Architect large file uploads
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a large-file upload architecture with multipart uploads, resumability, validation, metadata storage, and secure delivery controls.

output_examples.input: A user uploads profile images through a server endpoint.
output_examples.output: The response recommends magic-byte validation, a strict size cap, generated filenames, and post-upload image optimization.

output_examples.input: A team wants browser uploads directly to S3.
output_examples.output: The response outlines short-lived presigned URLs, expected size checks, safe object keys, and no-cache handling for private links.

output_examples.input: A private document URL is returned by an API.
output_examples.output: The response flags caching risk and recommends short expiry, no-store headers, and stronger signed delivery controls.

best_practices: Validate actual file content before trusting names or headers.
Generate storage keys instead of using user filenames directly.
Use direct cloud uploads for large files when possible.
anti_patterns: Do not accept unlimited upload sizes.
Do not serve private presigned URLs through cacheable responses.
Do not rely only on file extensions for safety decisions.

faq.question: Does this skill write upload code for a specific framework?
faq.answer: It gives patterns and examples that can be adapted to your framework.

faq.question: Can it help with S3 and Cloudflare R2?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers presigned URL patterns for both S3-compatible storage systems.

faq.question: Does it replace malware scanning?
faq.answer: No. It recommends validation basics, but dedicated malware scanning may still be required.

faq.question: Can it help prevent path traversal?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends basename handling, extension allowlists, and generated filenames.

faq.question: Is it useful for large uploads?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends streaming, direct uploads, and multipart upload strategies.

faq.question: Does it manage cloud credentials?
faq.answer: No. It does not configure IAM roles, bucket policies, or secret storage.
